$comment: WHERE EACH VENDORED CHECKER CAME FROM. A copy kept byte-identical can be diffed against
its source -- but only if the diff is against the SOURCE. On 2026-09-23 this repo vendored
the fence checker from a SIBLING repo's copy rather than the original and inherited a
49-line staleness that looked perfect in every comparison available here: three copies
agreeing is not confirmation when the thing they agree with is each other. The missing rule
was the one written because of this repo.
So each row records the source path, the source repo's commit at the time of copying, and
the sha256 of the bytes. The hash is checked by tests/test_vendored_sources.py, which
detects LOCAL drift; the source and commit are what let anyone holding both trees detect
the other direction, which no test inside a clone can do.
A row re-vendored later than the rest carries its own source_commit, which overrides the top-level one for that row.
